lastPrompt: when we generate pushes via forgemark we ingest all of this rubbish into our searches. what could be a strategy to avoid that? using a ref that is not head?

content.text:
Yes, pushing under a namespace outside `refs/heads/` is the cleanest client-side lever, and the code is close to supporting it. A few things worth weighing before picking it.

**Why a non-branch ref works.** Forge indexers, code search, CI triggers and branch UIs almost all key off `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*`. A ref like `refs/forgemark/fm…-c1-a0` still goes through the full receive-pack path on the server, so the benchmark still measures packfile unpack, ref CAS and hooks. It just never becomes a branch, so nothing downstream picks it up. It also sidesteps the "first push promotes a branch to HEAD and then the forge refuses to delete it" problem that the sweep currently has to special-case.

**The trade-offs:**

- **It changes what you measure.** If Entire does indexing or any post-receive work synchronously in the push path, non-branch refs skip that cost and the numbers get rosier than what a real agent pushing a branch would see. If it is async, push latency is unaffected but you stop generating the downstream load, which may or may not be something you want to benchmark.
- **Forge acceptance varies.** GitHub, GitLab and Gitea all accept arbitrary `refs/*` namespaces, but each reserves some (`refs/pull/*` on GitHub and Gitea, `refs/merge-requests/*`, `refs/keep-around/*`, `refs/pipelines/*` on GitLab). A dedicated name like `refs/forgemark/` avoids all of those. Whether Entire accepts it is something to confirm against your receive-pack.
- **Session strategy clones need a branch.** The clone and session paths clone `-base-ref`, which defaults to the remote default branch. Push-only runs are fine, but if a repo never gets a branch, the clone strategy needs an explicit base ref or a seeded repo.

**Forge-side alternatives** that keep the workload representative and only need Entire changes:

- **Exclude by author.** Every bench commit already uses the fixed `authorEmail` constant and `agent-N` author names, so the indexer could skip those commits outright.
- **Exclude by branch prefix.** Runs already take `-branch-prefix`, so Entire could treat `bench/` or similar as unindexed.
- **Exclude by repo.** A bench org or a per-repo "no search index" flag is the bluntest and most reliable option.

**If you want the ref-namespace route in forgemark**, the `refs/heads/` assumption lives in a handful of places: `DestRef` in `internal/bench/config.go`, the stale-ref regex and default-branch sparing in `internal/bench/cleanup.go`, the push refspecs in `agent.go` and `session.go`, and the error-normalizing `reRef` regex in `agent.go`. A `-ref-namespace` flag defaulting to `refs/heads/` would keep current behaviour and let you opt into a hidden namespace per run.

**My recommendation:** do both. Add the namespace flag so GitHub and GitLab comparisons stay clean without asking anything of those forges, and add the author-email exclusion on the Entire side so you can still run branch-shaped pushes against Entire when you want the full post-receive cost included.

content.text:
No. In the session strategy the only thing that stays a branch is the one you clone from, and that is the repo's real default branch which forgemark never writes to.

Two refs are in play per session:

- **Read side:** `cloneSession` clones the remote default branch, or `-base-ref`. That is pre-existing content like `main`. It would stay `refs/heads/...` and nothing forgemark does touches it.
- **Write side:** `runSessions` builds the destination as `a.ref` plus `-sN` and pushes with the refspec `+<local branch>:<that ref>`. Today `a.ref` comes from `DestRef`, which hardcodes `refs/heads/`. If `DestRef` emitted `refs/forgemark/...` instead, the session checkpoints would land at `refs/forgemark/fm…-c1-a0-s3`. The forge only sees the destination side of the refspec, so the fact that the local source is `refs/heads/master` or the cloned head is irrelevant to it.

So the session strategy needs no extra work beyond the namespace change in `DestRef` and the matching regexes in cleanup. The clone side keeps hitting a real branch, and the pushed checkpoints are hidden refs.

The caveat I raised earlier only applies to an unseeded repo. Today the first bench push to an empty repo creates a default branch, which later sessions clone. With a hidden namespace the repo stays unborn, so `cloneSession` takes its existing `ErrEmptyRemoteRepository` path and commits on an orphan with no read load. Against a repo seeded with a normal `main` that path never triggers.

Done. The change is on a new branch `feat/forgemark-ref-namespace` off `origin/main`, uncommitted so you can look it over. Build, vet, race tests and golangci-lint all pass.

**What changed**

- **New `-ref-namespace` flag**, default `refs/forgemark/`. `DestRef` now takes the namespace, and `Workload.Namespace()` normalizes it to one trailing slash. Validation rejects anything that is not `refs/<name>/` and blames the right flag.
- **Session refs inherit it** automatically, since they append `-sN` to the agent ref. No session-specific code changed.
- **Stale-ref sweep** anchors on the namespace plus prefix, so a run only cleans refs under its own namespace.
- **Error grouping** in `agent.go` collapses any `refs/...` ref, not just `refs/heads/`.
- **Server API** accepts `ref_namespace` in the workload spec and records the default on the run, so result docs say where refs went. The web form has a Ref namespace field prefilled with the default.
- **README** documents the flag, the reasoning, and the empty-repo consequence.

**Two things to be aware of**

- **Existing leftovers under `refs/heads/bench/` will no longer be swept** by default runs. One run with `-ref-namespace refs/heads/` against each bench repo cleans them up, after which they stop accumulating.
- **Empty repos stay empty** under the new default, so clone and session against an unseeded repo degrade to push-only. Seed a `main` where you want read load.

I did not touch `compare-local.sh` or the race preset. Both omit the field, so they pick up the default through the server.

records the effective namespace on the run so result docs say where
refs went. Under the default no bench push can create a branch, so an
empty repo stays empty and clone/session against it degrade to
push-only.

EOF

## Why

Every forgemark push to `refs/heads/*` triggers the target forge's post-receive pipeline: search ingestion, CI, webhooks, branch UI. On Entire that means paying for and rate-limiting search ingestion of random benchmark blobs. None of that work shows up in the push latency forgemark measures, since receive-pack does the same pack unpack, connectivity check and ref CAS for any ref.

## What

- **`-ref-namespace`** flag (and `ref_namespace` on the server API / web form), default **`refs/forgemark/`**. `DestRef` takes the namespace; `Workload.Namespace()` normalizes it. Validation requires `refs/<name>/` and blames the right flag.
- Session refs inherit it automatically (they append `-sN` to the agent ref).
- The stale-ref sweep anchors on namespace + prefix, so a run only cleans its own namespace.
- Error grouping collapses any `refs/...` ref, not just `refs/heads/`.
- The server records the effective namespace on the run so result docs say where refs went.
- README documents the flag, the reasoning, and the empty-repo consequence.

`-ref-namespace refs/heads/` restores branch pushes for anyone who wants to load the post-receive pipeline on purpose.

## Notes for operators

- Existing leftovers under `refs/heads/bench/` are no longer swept by default runs. One run with `-ref-namespace refs/heads/` per bench repo cleans them up.
- Under the default no bench push creates a branch, so an empty repo stays empty: clone/session against an unseeded repo degrade to push-only. Seed a `main` where you want read load.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet`, `go test -race ./...` and `golangci-lint run` all clean. New tests cover namespace normalization/validation, the sweep regex across namespaces, and error-message ref collapsing under the new default.

bench: record the ref namespace in results and keep sweeping refs/heads/

Two gaps the trail review found. Result docs (CLI format 1 and server
format 2) never stored where a run's pushes landed, so a refs/heads/ run
and a refs/forgemark/ run — different post-receive work on the forge —
would compare as equivalent in history. Doc.RefNamespace now records
it, the history row shows it, and docs written before the field existed
load as refs/heads/, the only place pushes could go back then.

The sweep was anchored on the current namespace alone, so upgrading
would have stranded every refs/heads/fm... leftover from earlier
versions in the advertisement — the history-dependence the sweep exists
to remove. It now always covers refs/heads/ too, under the same shape,
prefix and age guards, with the default-branch sparing unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q origin feat/forgemark-ref-namespace 2>&1 | tail -2
gh pr edit 18 --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Why

Every forgemark push to `refs/heads/*` triggers the target forge's post-receive pipeline: search ingestion, CI, webhooks, branch UI. That is paid-for, rate-limited work on the target, and none of it shows up in the push latency forgemark measures, since receive-pack does the same pack unpack, connectivity check and ref CAS for any ref.

## What

- **`-ref-namespace`** flag (and `ref_namespace` on the server API / web form), default **`refs/forgemark/`**. `DestRef` takes the namespace; `Workload.Namespace()` normalizes it. Validation requires `refs/<name>/` and blames the right flag.
- Session refs inherit it automatically (they append `-sN` to the agent ref).
- The stale-ref sweep anchors on namespace + prefix, and always also covers `refs/heads/`, where every pre-namespace forgemark pushed, so upgrading doesn't strand old leftovers in the advertisement. Same shape, prefix and age guards; default-branch sparing unchanged.
- Error grouping collapses any `refs/...` ref, not just `refs/heads/`.
- Result docs (CLI and server) record `ref_namespace`, and the history row shows it. Docs written before the field existed load as `refs/heads/`, so they don't read as equivalent to a `refs/forgemark/` run.
- README documents the flag, the reasoning, and the empty-repo consequence.

`-ref-namespace refs/heads/` restores branch pushes for anyone who wants to load the post-receive pipeline on purpose.

## Notes for operators

- Under the default no bench push creates a branch, so an empty repo stays empty: clone/session against an unseeded repo degrade to push-only. Seed a `main` where you want read load.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet`, `go test -race ./...` and `golangci-lint run` all clean. New tests cover namespace normalization/validation, the sweep regex across namespaces including the legacy one, result-doc round trip and legacy normalization, and error-message ref collapsing under the new default.

EOF

content.text:
Both findings are fixed, pushed, and resolved on the trail. The PR now has two commits and an updated description.

**The two findings and what changed**

- **Result docs did not record the namespace.** The reviewer was right, and my earlier PR text overstated this. Only the live status payload carried it, not the persisted doc. Now both the CLI format 1 writer and the server format 2 writer store `ref_namespace`, the history row displays it, and docs written before the field existed load as `refs/heads/` since that was the only place pushes could go. The CLI banner also prints the namespace at run start.
- **The sweep stranded legacy `refs/heads/` leftovers.** The regex now always alternates `refs/heads/` alongside the configured namespace, with the same shape, prefix and age guards. Default-branch sparing is unchanged, which matters because a legacy run may have promoted a bench ref to HEAD on an empty repo. Other custom namespaces are still never crossed into.

**Verification:** build, vet, race tests and golangci-lint are clean. New tests cover the legacy-namespace alternation including capture-group position, result-doc round trip, and legacy normalization for both doc formats.
